title: The Hollow Salt
premise: In the salt-locked valley of Hollowmere, where magic cannot cross the brine flats, Ulyana Thackeray survives by stealing memories from travelers and selling them back to the grieving. When a scholar arrives carrying a century-old book of prophecies that names her as the 'Salt-Bearer' who will either seal or shatter the ancient war-god Vessik, Ulyana learns the valley's magiclessness is not protection but a prison built by her own ancestors to contain their crime. Hunted by the scholar's order and betrayed by the man she trusted with tonight's date, she must journey beyond the brine into a world of living magic to find the truth of what her family buried. In the end, Ulyana chooses neither prophecy: she dissolves the god by returning his stolen memories to him, at the cost of her own past, becoming the valley's nameless keeper while Hollowmere finally opens its gates.
about_author: Ivo Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal customs house before turning to fiction. They write about memory, borders, and the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Brine Market
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the eve of a rare date with the charming cartographer Dain, Ulyana works the market, lifting a widow's memory of her husband's face for coin. The chapter establishes her rules—never steal pain, never leave the valley—and ends when she notices a stranger watching her with a book chained to his wrist. Beat: wary competence shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Name in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The stranger, Scholar Emrys Vale, corners her: the prophecy book names 'the Salt-Bearer, born of Thackeray line' and dates her death in forty days. She steals a page from his mind to verify it and finds her own face sketched a century ago. Beat: vertigo—the invisible life revealed as an observed one.

chapters.title: What Dain Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Her date with Dain curdles when she accidentally reads his surface memories and finds he was sent by Vale's order to confirm her existence. Confronted, Dain admits half-truths; she banishes him but keeps the token he gave her. Beat: betrayal, and the first crack in her belief that staying small means staying safe.

chapters.title: The Ancestors' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interludes from the ledger itself. Searching her grandmother's sealed cellar, Ulyana finds records showing the Thackerays didn't flee magic—they imprisoned the war-god Vessik beneath the valley, erasing the town's memory of the war. The brine is a lock, and her bloodline its wardens. Beat: horror of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Fewer Now
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Vale reveals his order wants Ulyana dead before the prophesied date, believing her death re-seals the god; he has defected to warn her instead. Pursuers arrive in Hollowmere, and the first traveler in years crosses the flats without losing his magic—the seal is weakening. Beat: reluctant alliance forged under deadline.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fleeing the order's hunters, Ulyana and Vale cross the brine flats at night. Outside the valley, magic floods her senses—every stolen memory she carries begins speaking, and the land remembers her ancestors' march to war. She vomits, weeps, keeps walking. Beat: overwhelming cost of leaving home.

chapters.title: The God Who Was Robbed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the drowned temple, they learn Vessik was no conqueror but a memory-keeper god whom the Thackerays lobotomized to end a war, stealing his divinity to build the valley's peace. Ulyana realizes her gift is a splinter of his stolen power. Beat: moral inversion—her family were the villains of the old story.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Temple
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The order's hunters storm the temple; Dain, sent to redeem himself, turns his blade against them to save Ulyana and is gravely wounded. Vale sacrifices himself holding the stair, telling Ulyana the prophecy's second line: 'The bearer chooses which hollow fills.' Beat: grief, sacrifice, and clarity of choice.

chapters.title: The Return of Everything
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Beneath Hollowmere, Ulyana faces the hollowed god and does what no prophecy imagined: she gives back every memory she has ever stolen, then her own—all of it, her childhood, her mother, Dain—to make Vessik whole enough to dissolve peacefully rather than rise in wrath. Beat: climax; self-erasure as the ultimate act of justice outside law.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Hollow Salt
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The valley wakes with open gates and no memory of why it was ever closed; the brine has become ordinary sea-salt. A woman with no past tends the flats, content, occasionally visited by Dain who tells her their story each time, and each time she chooses to begin again. Beat: bittersweet resolution—memory lost, justice kept.
